title: A Methodological Study on Sensor-Based Measurement of Head Movement Parameters: A Comparative Study Between an Ear Sensor and 3D Motion Analysis in Healthy Study Participants
summary:
This study investigates whether a small motion sensor attached to the ear can reliably track head movements during everyday activities. Healthy participants perform various tasks such as walking, speaking, and making orientation head movements. The measurements from the ear sensor are compared with those from a high-precision camera system.
In the long term, the technology is intended to help better track movement disorders in people with e.g. Parkinson’s disease during daily life. Unlike previous sensors worn on the wrist or back, an ear sensor could be worn continuously, for example, integrated into hearing aids or eyeglass frames. This would also allow for the tracking of movements while sitting.

interventions.name:
Healthy participants aged 18 to 35 (N=20).
All parameters are measured during a single session.
Participants perform standardized tasks based on everyday situations, including head movements for orientation, speech, and walking tasks. The sensor data recorded by the ear-mounted sensor is compared

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- German as a native language or adequate knowledge of German
- Sufficient vision (corrected with contact lenses or glasses if necessary)
Exclusion criteria:
- Pre-existing neurological/vestibular conditions: Known disorders of the sense of balance, dizziness, or diagnosed neurological conditions
- Acute injuries: Injuries or surgeries involving the musculoskeletal system (cervical spine, hip, knee) that impair natural gait or head motor function
- Substance-related factors: Use of medications that affect reaction time or motor function
